title: Finite sums for a nonarchimedean function, including a unique dominant summand
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $N:K\to\mathbf R$ satisfy $N(x+y)\le\max(N(x),N(y))$ and $N(-x)=N(x)$ for all $x,y\in K$. Let $I$ be any set, $S\subset I$ a finite nonempty subset, and $a:I\to K$. Then $N(\sum_{i\in S}a_i)\le\max_{i\in S}N(a_i)$. Moreover, if $k\in S$ and $N(a_i)<N(a_k)$ for every $i\in S\setminus\{k\}$, then $N(\sum_{i\in S}a_i)=N(a_k)$. No nonnegativity or definiteness assumption on $N$ is imposed.

from.place: Historical analytic input supporting the normalization chain from lem-trf-local-term-locality, through Temkin Theorem 3.5.5 Step 2: Power-bounded elements are integral over a presentation unit ball. This is below the node level, not a replacement of the current contracting-correspondence unit proof. Supporting analytic input: Supremum seminorm estimates on affinoid algebras. The unit criterion used to construct a maximal point of the auxiliary hypersurface 1-Yf=0 in the proof of the Tate Gauss/supremum comparison. Bosch Section 1.2, the Gauss-norm discussion preceding Proposition 3, printed pp.8-9 (PDF pp.9-10); prerequisite of the unit-criterion argument. Finite ultrametric Cauchy-coefficient estimates and evaluation at a unique dominant summand in the Gauss multiplicativity proof.
